I am an old woman, almost seventy, farming this small piece of land behind our compound here in the South East. My husband's people gave us this land long ago, and I plant my yam and cassava together with some melon and maize like my mother taught me. I have no money for the chemical fertilizer they sell in town — it is too costly and my plot is small — so I use the droppings from our goats and the ash from the kitchen fire. My children help me when they can, but mostly it is me bending my back on this land.
